adjudication.one_line: Vegetation greening in a wet 2026 season: a 12-pixel bbox cut from a ragged SW-NE green swath; siblings 172 m and 306 m away already closed the same way.
adjudication.summary: before.png and after.png show the same mottled shrub-on-bare-soil plateau inside the 115 x 54 m box in both years, with no new object, edge or bright surface; hires.png (Esri, 2025-05-30, pre-onset) and all six wayback_strip.png releases from 2014 to 2026 show only shrub clumps and faint old tracks, nothing built. falsecolor_after.png shows a ragged, lobate green band several hundred metres long running SW-NE through the box, absent in falsecolor_before.png, and difference.png shows the NDVI rise spanning that whole swath while the brightness panel is near zero at the box. timeseries.png shows inside and ring tracking identically through 2024-2025, a joint snow spike on 2026-01-03, and then the footprint staying slightly greener (inside-minus-ring NDVI +0.017 to +0.032, NBR +0.04 to +0.06) through 2026 while brightness contrast is unchanged within 0.01. The panel concluded unanimously (3 of 3 refuted, high confidence) that this is interannual greening of sparse shrub-steppe in a shallow hollow during a wetter 2026, the same regional response that produced eight sibling candidates across 37 km, including OC0011 at 172 m and OC0007 at 306 m with the identical onset window, both already closed as natural:regional_pattern. OC0014 escaped that rule only because its 4,800 m2 area is exactly 12 pixels at 20 m and the shape metrics (4 corners, rectangularity 0.8) describe the bounding box rather than any shape seen in an image; the Landsat confirmation is the same NBR greening measured twice (0.053 vs 0.054), not independent evidence of an installation.
adjudication.explanation: Natural vegetation greening (regional wet-year response, 2026) of sparse shrub-steppe on the Ustyurt plateau, locally stronger along a shallow drainage hollow; the footprint is a bounding-box fragment of a continuous SW-NE greening swath. The spectral signature (d_ndvi +0.106, d_nbr +0.158, d_brightness -0.022, d_swir -0.039, zero brightness contrast change against the ring) is vegetation, not construction, and no structure, pad, pit or new track appears in hires.png or any Wayback release.
adjudication.next_step: Any sub-metre image acquired after May 2026 (next Esri/Maxar refresh) of 43.4454 N 56.1979 E showing only denser shrub/grass in the footprint would close it outright; without new imagery, re-run the natural:regional_pattern check with the regular-outline exception disabled for blobs under ~20 detection pixels (or with the shape computed from the change mask instead of its bbox), merging OC0007, OC0011 and OC0014 into one footprint, and check the July 2027 Sentinel-2 composite: a shrinking inside-minus-ring NDVI excess in a drier year confirms vegetation.

adjudication.one_line: Prospecting or borrow pits with pale spoil dug beside a dirt track in 2023-24; seen directly in hires.png and the 2026 Wayback mosaic.
adjudication.summary: Sentinel-2 before.png shows a uniform brown bare slope immediately west of a north-south dirt track; after.png shows a bright pale patch about 150 x 95 m filling the footprint against that track, with a new straight pale track running east from the junction. hires.png (Esri, picture dated 2025-03-05, after onset) resolves the patch into an excavated area of pale subsoil with several dark pits separated by spoil heaps, a short spur from the track carrying two small vehicle-sized objects, and a turning loop; wayback_strip.png shows undisturbed ground in every mosaic release from 2014 through 2023-10-11 and the same pit cluster in the 2026-05-28 release. The 32-scene series (timeseries.png) shows inside-minus-ring brightness climbing stepwise from about 0 in mid-2023 to +0.07 by 2024-02 and holding near +0.05 through 2025, with NBR rising and SWIR flat (d_swir +0.003), the signature of exposed dry pale regolith rather than water, fire or snow; Landsat independently confirms the brightening (shift 0.035 vs noise 0.004) while SAR, thermal and night lights are null, as expected for shallow digging. All three sceptics (human activity, natural processes, artefacts) independently identified small-scale excavation in a known small-mining district (Margarita mine 3.4 km away), and the panel agrees: the cause is directly visible at 1 m resolution, so the candidate is explained.
adjudication.explanation: Small-scale earthworks: a cluster of excavation pits (prospecting workings or borrow scrapes) with pale spoil heaps, opened on the west side of an existing dirt track (OSM way 111564066) between about 2023-08 and 2024-02, together with a newly graded straight east-west access track from the same junction; the brightening is freshly exposed pale subsurface material.
adjudication.next_step: Not required for the verdict. If an operator is wanted: query Chile's SERNAGEOMIN Catastro Minero at -25.3620, -69.9862 for a concession (pedimento or manifestacion) registered in 2023-2024, or obtain one dated commercial scene (Planet or Maxar) from 2023-08 to 2024-02 showing machinery opening the pits.

adjudication.one_line: Drying of a high-Andean wetland (vega) meadow patch, part of a strip-wide 2023-24 moisture decline that partly recovered in 2025; no mark on the ground.
adjudication.summary: before.png and after.png (Sentinel-2, 10 m) show a dark-green wetland strip crossing bare Puna desert at 3,770 m with the yellow box on the strip's southern edge; inside the box the two composites are near-identical apart from a slightly browner, smaller dark wet patch at the SW corner, and no new line, pad or spot appears. hires.png (Esri, 2023-03-15, before onset) shows only dense cushion-plant mat with pale dry patches inside the box and no track, pit, structure or object; wayback_strip.png shows the same patch swinging between dense and sparse green across releases from 2014 to 2026. difference.png shows the brightening (red) running along the whole ~1 km strip and the NDVI loss (brown) in the box matched by a larger brown blob ~150 m WNW, so the footprint is one cell of a wetland-wide moisture change. The per-scene series (29 scenes) has no step: inside NBR slides from 0.441 (2023-05-13) to 0.298 (2024-04-07), then recovers to 0.413 (2024-06), 0.424 (2024-12), 0.601 (2025-03) and 0.434 (2025-06), with the ring moving in parallel; the brief itself notes that per-scene values do not separate before from after (shift -0.075 vs noise 0.112, 5 of 11 later scenes show the change), the dossier's own composites give an inside NBR change of only -0.045 (0.379 to 0.335) against the claimed -0.158, and the Landsat 'confirmation' recovers monotonically (NBR 0.168, 0.187, 0.207, 0.248). All three sceptics (human activity, natural processes, artefacts) independently refuted the candidate with high confidence, converging on the same ordinary cause, and the panel agrees: the change is a reversible drying of living wetland vegetation (SWIR +0.133 dominates, surface_water sub-check drying_signature=true, flat_basin=true, WorldCover 85% grass inside vs 90% bare around), exaggerated into a 'step' by comparing a lush early-May 2023 with a dry early-May 2024 in three-date composites; the landing_trace shape metrics are those of the 8-pixel bounding box (footprint_source bbox, straight_edge_fraction 0.0), not of a real outline.
adjudication.explanation: Interannual drying of a high-Andean wetland meadow (vega/bofedal cushion-plant mat) at the southern edge of a spring-fed vega strip: the saturated core inside the box shrank and the mat lost water through the 2023 dry season and the weak 2023-24 wet season, then partly recovered in 2025. The same decline covers the whole strip (difference.png) and both sensors record a dip-and-recover, not a persistent mark. The detector's three-date early-May composites turned this gradual, reversible moisture fluctuation into an apparent abrupt step (step_snr 8) that the full per-scene series does not support. Whether the water deficit was rainfall, grazing from the Cavi puesto 1.1 km away, or abstraction at Proyecto Lindero 4.9 km away cannot be told from imagery; none is exotic.
adjudication.next_step: A Sentinel-2 all-season per-scene NBR/NDWI series through May 2026 for the footprint, the larger NDVI-loss patch ~150 m WNW and the ring: all three following the same dip-and-recover trajectory, with 2026 values back inside the 2018-2023 Apr-May range (NBR 0.43-0.50), closes it as a transient wetland moisture low. A single cloud-free sub-metre image from mid-2024 showing the mat intact with no scar, cut or object would close it outright; CHIRPS/ERA5 precipitation anomalies for the 2023-24 wet season would name the driver.

adjudication.one_line: Freshly graded rectangular pad (~90 x 60 m) built against an existing track with a new spur, Aug-Sep 2023, Salar de Arizaro margin: earthworks, likely exploration pad.
adjudication.summary: before.png (Sentinel-2 median May-Jul 2023) and hires.png (Esri, WorldView-3, 2023-07-21, one day before the last-absent date) show only a faint NNE-SSW vehicle track crossing the footprint box on uniform bare alluvial-fan ground; after.png (Nov 2023-Feb 2024) shows a crisp, straight-edged pale rectangle sitting directly against the west side of that track, the track itself brighter and wider, and a new straight spur leaving the junction westward to a small bright patch about 400-700 m away. difference.png shows the rectangle and the three straight lines converging on it as the strongest brightenings in the 2 km panel, with the NDVI panel flat; falsecolor_after.png shows the pad pale in SWIR1/NIR/red, i.e. dry exposed light subsoil, not water or vegetation. The brief's shape metrics (4 corners, rectangularity 0.87, 104 x 62 m, orientation 0 deg), the clean single step in timeseries.png (inside ~0.05 above the ring in every scene from 2023-09-27 through mid-2025; NBR -0.10 to +0.08-0.11), Landsat confirmation and a SAR contrast drop of 0.83 dB (smoother surface) all fit a bladed platform. All three sceptics (human activity, natural processes, data artefacts) refuted the candidate with high confidence and the panel agrees: this is ordinary earthworks, a graded pad with an access track, of the kind common for lithium-brine exploration on the Salar de Arizaro margin (a sibling pad, SW-B19-PUNA-OC0014, appeared 3.7 km north in the same period). The specific operator and purpose are inferred, not seen; the earthworks themselves are seen.
adjudication.explanation: Human earthworks: a graded rectangular platform (about 90 x 60 m) bladed on the west side of pre-existing OSM track 399502073, with the track re-graded and a new westward spur track cut to a short-lived second worksite, between 2023-07-22 and 2023-09-27. Scraping the darker desert pavement exposed pale fine subsoil (visible/NIR/SWIR1 brightening, NDVI and NDWI unchanged). Most likely a mineral-exploration (lithium brine) drill or camp pad on the eastern margin of Salar de Arizaro.
adjudication.next_step: Any sub-metre image of -25.0977, -67.6248 acquired after September 2023 (Maxar, Airbus, Planet SkySat, or an Esri/Google mosaic refresh; the Esri Wayback record still ends at the 2023-07-21 picture here) to show blade/berm edges, tyre marks, a drill collar or camp equipment on the pad; or the Salta provincial mining cadastre / environmental-impact register for a 2023 exploration permit covering this part of the Arizaro margin, naming the operator.

adjudication.one_line: Earthworks beside an unpaved road on the Salar de Arizaro margin: scraped pad, spoil and a pit/loop visible in 2023 high-res imagery, absent in 2021.
adjudication.summary: before.png (median of 2021-05 to 2022-03) shows uniform brown bare ground with only a faint unpaved track crossing the yellow box, about 100 m west of the pale evaporite margin of Salar de Arizaro; after.png (2023-05/06) shows a pale blotch filling the box east of the track, a second blotch just north-east, a third small bright spot about 200 m south-west at a track junction, and a sharper road. hires.png (Esri/WV03, 2023-07-21, 13 months after onset) resolves the box as a scraped patch of pale disturbed ground on the east shoulder of OSM way 241543244 with a spoil tail along the road, a pale rectangular pad with a dark object at its corner to the north-east, and a roughly 100 m pale-rimmed oval depression or turning loop abutting the box; wayback_strip.png shows none of this in the 2014, 2016, 2019 and 2021-10-13 releases and all of it in the 2023-10-11 and 2026-08-05 releases, bracketing the Sentinel-2 onset. The spectra are those of freshly exposed dry pale subsoil (d_brightness +0.049, d_swir +0.058, d_ndvi -0.004, d_nbr +0.029), the footprint brightened while the surrounding salt crust darkened (difference.png), and the step persists for four years with 12 of 12 later scenes agreeing and Landsat confirming; the 2022-06-07 scene is a dark anomalous acquisition shared by footprint and ring in timeseries.png, so the clean onset bracket is 2022-05-05 to 2022-07-19. All three sceptics (human activity, natural processes, artefacts) independently refuted the candidate with high confidence on the same evidence, differing only in how they describe the geometry of the pit versus pad outside the box. The panel concludes the change is ordinary mechanical earthworks beside an existing road in an active mining and exploration district (three OSM landuse=industrial polygons 2.0 to 2.4 km away; Lindero and Rio Grande mines 11 to 13 km), most likely an exploration or borrow working; the exact purpose is inferred, the earthwork itself is directly seen.
adjudication.explanation: Ordinary earthworks on the east shoulder of an existing unpaved road (OSM way 241543244) at the western margin of Salar de Arizaro: a scraped or graded patch with spoil inside the footprint, plus an adjoining pale rectangular pad and a roughly 100 m pale-rimmed oval depression or turning loop just north-east of the box, all connected by vehicle tracks. Directly visible in hires.png (WV03, 2023-07-21) and in the Esri Wayback 2023-10-11 and 2026-08-05 releases, absent in the 2021-10-13 release; consistent with mineral or brine exploration pad/sump work or road-maintenance borrow in an active mining district. The precise purpose is inferred; the mechanical disturbance is seen.
adjudication.next_step: A dated sub-metre image from the onset bracket (Planet or Maxar archive, 2022-05-05 to 2022-07-19) showing machinery, fresh spoil or a drill rig at -25.1072, -67.6410; or a Salta provincial mining cadastre lookup for exploration permits or drilling notices on the west shore of Salar de Arizaro near Vega Chascha in 2022, naming the operator of the three landuse=industrial sites 2 km away. Either would convert the inferred purpose into a documented one; the earthwork itself needs no further confirmation.

adjudication.one_line: Fresh pale sand/silt lobe deposited at a wadi-fan apex in late Aug 2025 (flood splay or wind-blown sand); no structure in any image.
adjudication.summary: before.png and after.png (Sentinel-2, Sep-Oct 2024 vs Sep 2025) show the same pale sand tongue at the head of a south-draining wadi fan between dark sandstone outcrops; after onset the tongue is marginally brighter with no new edge, object or shadow, and difference.png shows a soft brightening of +0.02 to +0.04 in the north of the box feathering into a fan-wide +0.01 to +0.02, with NDVI flat. hires.png (Esri, acquired 2023-09-09, pre-change) and all six wayback_strip.png releases (2014 to 2026-05-28, the last identical to the 2023 picture) show only braided wash channels and bare sand, nothing built. The per-scene series in dossier.json confirms the step: inside-minus-ring NBR contrast 0.034-0.052 for the 17 good scenes to 2025-08-06 (the 0.067 point on 2025-01-28 is an S2C scene read without its radiometric offset), then 0.011-0.021 for all 13 scenes from 2025-09-05 to 2026-11-24, with brightness contrast rising from about 0.026 to 0.033. All three sceptics refuted the candidate and converged on one cause: a lobe of fresh pale sediment at the gully mouth, whose change vector matches the bright-sand-minus-dark-rock endmember (cosine 0.978), whose 10 m shape is a soft teardrop with a tail down the wash rather than the rectangle implied by the 20 m bounding-box metrics (footprint_source 'bbox', about 10x7 pixels), which appeared in a single step between the 26 and 31 August 2025 passes while the 31 August scene shows a basin-wide wet-ground/cloud transient, and which has a same-vector sibling (OC0047) 8.8 km away in the same season. SAR (-0.30 dB, noise 0.23) and thermal (-0.55 K, noise 0.63) did not change, as expected for a thin sediment sheet and not for a built object, so the panel records an ordinary sediment deposit; whether a flash flood or wind delivered it is not resolved and does not need to be.
adjudication.explanation: Fresh pale sand/silt deposited as a lobe at the apex of a sand-filled wadi fan on the Gilf Kebir margin between 26 and 31 August 2025, most likely a flash-flood splay from the feeder gully to the north (the 31 Aug Sentinel-2 scene shows a basin-wide wetting/cloud transient), with wind-blown sand as the alternative delivery; the 'installation' shape signature comes from bounding-box metrics on a 10x7 pixel blob at 20 m, not from the changed pixels.
adjudication.next_step: A sub-metre image acquired after 5 September 2025 of 23.1937 N 26.0002 E (Maxar, Planet SkySat, or an Esri Wayback release with a post-2025 acquisition date; the 2026-05-28 release still shows the 2023 picture): a smooth sediment lobe or fresh sand ripples at the gully mouth with no tracks confirms deposition, while tracks, a graded pad or pits would reopen it. Secondary: IMERG or CHIRPS daily rainfall for 26-31 Aug 2025 at 23.2 N 26.0 E to confirm the storm, and fix the earthsearch:boa_offset_applied handling that corrupted the 2025-01-28 S2C scene in the series.

adjudication.summary: before.png (median of 2023-04-25 to 2023-08-13) shows uniform orange desert in the yellow box, faintly gridded into plots, with the dark dual carriageway of the Luxor-Aswan Western Road about 150-170 m to the east; after.png (median of 2024-05-19 to 2024-09-06) shows a bright cream patch filling most of the box plus new blue-grey roadside patches about 200 m north, and difference.png shows the footprint as an isolated compact brightening block (+0.04 and more) with only a weak NDVI dip. hires.png (Esri, acquired 2025-05-07, 1.09 m) resolves the box as a pale graded rectangle with an access track running north-east to the road, and a 0.54 m zoom chip of the same image shows a white-roofed shed about 25 x 10 m, two or three small blue-roofed cabins, a roughly 40 m berm or wall casting a shadow, a cluster of planted trees, tyre tracks and blue-grey stained ground: a small desert worksite or contractor yard. wayback_strip.png shows the spot as undisturbed desert in the releases published 2014, 2017, 2019, 2022 and 2023-12-07 and the same graded yard in the 2026-05-28 release; OSM already maps a 161 m highway=service way (1230530633) touching the footprint, with the Cairo-Abu Simbel high-speed railway under construction 278 m away. timeseries.png shows inside-footprint brightness tracking the ring until mid-2023 and then ramping over about nine months (inside-minus-ring contrast +0.010 in Aug 2023 to +0.100 in May 2024) with NBR rising in step, a staged build-up rather than a single event, confirmed independently by Landsat (+0.041) and present in 12 of 12 later Sentinel-2 scenes; the spectra (d_brightness +0.084, d_nbr +0.082, d_swir +0.016, d_ndvi -0.022) are those of pale dry exposed or compacted fill, not burn, water or snow, on a flat (0.9 deg) hyperarid plain. All three sceptics (human activity, natural processes, artefacts) independently refuted the candidate with high confidence on the same evidence, and the panel concludes it is an ordinary graded construction yard beside a trunk road in an active construction corridor; the buildings, berm and track are directly seen, the yard's exact purpose is inferred.
adjudication.explanation: Ordinary earthworks: a small desert worksite or contractor yard graded on a roadside plot between about August 2023 and May 2024, beside the Luxor-Aswan Western Road (trunk, 163 m) and 278 m from the Cairo-Abu Simbel high-speed railway under construction. The Esri image of 2025-05-07 (hires.png and its 0.54 m zoom) shows the graded pale pad with a white-roofed shed, blue-roofed cabins, a berm, planted trees, tyre tracks and an access track to the road, the track already mapped in OSM as service way 1230530633 touching the footprint; the five Wayback releases through 2023-12-07 show undisturbed desert there. The brightening is exposed pale compacted fill or subsoil. The yard's specific purpose (HSR contractor yard, land-reclamation plot or well site) is inferred.
adjudication.next_step: A single dated image between September 2023 and May 2024 (a Sentinel-2 chip from 2023-09-27, 2023-11-11 or 2024-01-30, or a Planet/Maxar scene) at 24.5329 N 32.7294 E to watch the pad, berm and buildings appear stage by stage; or the OSM history of service way 1230530633 and any later landuse tag to name the yard's purpose. Neither is needed to exclude an extraordinary cause, which the 2025-05-07 Esri image already does.

adjudication.one_line: Regional drying/bleaching of a takyr drainage hollow between summer 2024 and 2025; the box is 8 pixels of a 13-17 ha brightening; no mark at 0.86 m.
adjudication.summary: before.png (median of 2024-07-02 to 2024-10-15) shows the yellow box on mid-toned mottled ground at the southern tip of a dark, finger-like tongue that trails from a drainage line to the north-east, with a bright pan about 300 m to the west; in after.png (2025-06-29 to 2025-08-31) the tongue has turned pale, a pale lobe runs from the pan through the box to the north-east, and the box interior is indistinguishable from the paler ground around it. difference.png shows the brightening as a dendritic, drainage-following network covering roughly a third of the 1.5 km panel, with the box at the southern edge of one of several large red blobs and near-zero NDVI change at the box; timeseries.png shows the footprint and its ring tracking each other through the whole record, both jumping bright in June 2025 with the footprint only a few hundredths above its ring afterwards and greener than it in 2026. hires.png (Esri WorldView-3, 2025-09-10, 0.86 m, three months after first detection) shows only mottled pale pan floor with scattered shrub clumps inside the box, no track, pad, pit, spoil, scorch or object, and wayback_strip.png shows the same tongue-and-pan setting in every release from 2014 to 2026. All three sceptics refuted the candidate: in fresh same-scene composites the footprint's change (+0.046 brightness, +0.043 NBR, +0.003 NDVI) matches its 60-120 m ring to within about 0.005, the adjacent dark tongue changed more than the footprint (NBR -0.086 to +0.018), and the connected region brightening the same way measures 13-17 ha against a 0.32 ha footprint. The pipeline's 'isolated, 0.1%' crowding figure is computed on the step-test mask (optical_change._blobs), not on the raw change field, so it missed a neighbourhood-wide surface-state shift; the detection is a statistical sliver of a regional change, not a discrete mark.
adjudication.explanation: Interannual surface-state change of a shallow takyr/sor drainage hollow on the Ustyurt plain: a dark, moist floor in the wetter 2024 season bleached to a pale crust in the drier 2025 season, together with the drainage-following network of low ground across the surrounding square kilometre. The 8-pixel footprint is the piece of that regional brightening whose history was quiet enough to pass the step test; the 2025-09-10 0.86 m image shows no disturbance at it.
adjudication.next_step: Recompute the widespread-change/crowding test on the raw per-pixel 2024-to-2025 brightness and NBR difference at 10 m (connected region touching the footprint, expected 13-17 ha) and feed that into the pipeline; optionally a March-June 2025 per-scene Sentinel-2 MNDWI/SWIR series over the dark tongue to show the floor stood wet before bleaching. No further imagery of the footprint is needed: the 2025-09-10 WorldView-3 view already shows no mark.

adjudication.one_line: Drought browning of an intact mesquite thicket below a stock tank; the whole scene browned the same way and 2023 1 m imagery shows no mark.
adjudication.summary: before.png (autumn 2020) and after.png (autumn 2022) show the 74 m footprint on the south-east tip of a dense shrub thicket immediately downstream of a crescent-shaped earthen livestock tank; the dark vegetation finger is present in both composites and the whole 1.5 km scene is browner after. hires.png (Esri, 2023-04-21, a year after present_from) shows the box filled with intact shrub canopy cut by one thin pale NW-SE line, and wayback_strip.png shows that same thicket and line unchanged in every release from 2014-02 to 2026-08, so no clearing, pit, pad, scar or structure appeared. difference.png shows NDVI decrease across almost the entire panel, strongest on every vegetated drainage, with the box one of many browned patches; the only increase is a teal rim on the tank margin. The stored per-scene series gives inside-vs-ring NDVI correlation 0.966 over 31 scenes, an inside/ring ratio of 1.45 before and 1.31 after (ranges overlap), and inside re-greening to 0.351 on 2022-09-22; the footprint (0.3165 to 0.2248, x0.71) and surroundings (0.2004 to 0.1355, x0.68) fell in the same proportion. The panel (three sceptics, all refuted, high confidence) concluded the detector's absolute-NDVI step on late-April composites picked out the densest vegetation in a landscape-wide dry-season browning between a green April 2021 and a dry April 2022, with two sibling candidates 3.8 and 4.7 km away changing the same way that year; fire, earthwork and a processing artefact are excluded.
adjudication.explanation: Drought-driven loss of dry-season foliage in a phreatophyte mesquite thicket growing below a man-made earthen stock tank (bordo), part of a landscape-wide 2022 browning in the Bolson de Mapimi. The detector compares late-April composites year to year and flagged the footprint because its baseline NDVI is the highest in the panel, so the largest absolute drop fell there; the relative change matches the surroundings (same x0.7 decline, inside/ring correlation 0.966) and the shrubs are intact and still green up every wet season. The Landsat confirmation is the same browning seen by a second optical sensor, not an independent surface event.
adjudication.next_step: Re-run the step test on the inside/ring NDVI ratio across the 2018-2026 April composites: a ratio that stays near 1.3-1.5 and recovers in wetter springs confirms landscape browning. A CHIRPS or CONAGUA rainfall series for winter 2020-21 versus 2021-22 would confirm the wet-then-dry spring sequence. No sub-metre image of the onset window is needed, since the 2023-04-21 Esri picture already shows the thicket intact.

adjudication.one_line: Real ~1 ha loss of sparse spinifex cover on a Gibson Desert dune crest, Nov 2024, leaving bright red sand; agent (small fire likeliest) not directly seen.
adjudication.summary: before.png (Oct-Dec 2023 median) shows the footprint as unremarkable mottled red sandplain; after.png (Dec 2024-Jan 2025 median) shows a slightly brighter, smoother patch filling the box, and difference.png shows one isolated NE-SW blob of +0.02 to +0.04 brightness and about -0.03 NDVI with nothing comparable in the 1 km view. hires.png (Esri, picture dated 2025-08-02, after onset) shows a bare pale-sand patch about 100-130 m by 60-80 m with lobate soft edges and several surviving dark shrubs inside, sitting on a pale WNW-ESE dune-crest band, with no vehicle track, straight edge, spoil or structure anywhere in the 600 m view; wayback_strip.png shows the box vegetated like its surroundings in the 2014-2023 releases and bare only in the 2026 release. timeseries.png and the dossier series show inside brightness stepping about +0.03 above the ring after the onset and staying there to Sept 2026 (14 of 14 later scenes, Landsat shift 0.025 vs noise 0.003), while inside NBR keeps the same ~0.03 offset below the ring it had before, so no charred phase is recorded; two sceptics bracketed the onset to 2024-11-12..11-24 from individual scenes. The panel (3 of 3 refuting) concluded the detection is sound and the change is an ordinary loss of sparse vegetation exposing bright sand, but disagreed on the agent: two favoured a small self-extinguishing spinifex fire in the November storm season (MODIS 500 m/1 km products cannot see a ~1 ha burn), one favoured mechanical scraping or aeolian stripping. Because no hotspot, char, track or blade mark was observed, the cause is likely but not shown, so the verdict is probably ordinary rather than explained.
adjudication.explanation: Loss of roughly 0.6-1.9 ha of sparse spinifex and shrub cover on a linear-dune crest inside the Gibson Desert Nature Reserve between 2024-11-12 and 2024-11-24, exposing bright red sand that has stayed bare since (d_brightness +0.037, d_swir +0.114, d_ndvi -0.032; hires.png and wayback_strip.png show the vegetation gone). Most plausibly a small, self-extinguishing spinifex fire during the November dry-storm season, in a landscape that context.png shows to be a fire-scar mosaic; mechanical clearing is disfavoured by the lobate edges and the absence of any track or straight edge at 1 m, and wind stripping by the 12-day onset and the centroid fixed to within 10 m for 20 months. The ignition or agent itself was not captured in any available image.
adjudication.next_step: A VIIRS 375 m active-fire lookup (VNP14IMG / VJ114IMG via FIRMS with a map key) for -24.678, 126.144 between 2024-11-12 and 2024-11-24: a hotspot would confirm a small fire outright. Failing that, any Planet or Maxar scene from 13-25 Nov 2024 showing a charred/ash-grey patch versus blade marks or vehicle tracks at the footprint, or the WA DBCA fire-history and DMIRS Program-of-Work records for the reserve in November 2024.
